   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}

## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions

**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else
default`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or
`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for "precondition not met." Downstream
theorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the
theorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the
obligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the
function. See issue [#495], related to [#307].

### Why it's bad

The signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a
non-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about "the output" is
proved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a
later theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition
type-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original
precondition failed.

The paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:
"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`." The Lean should
match.

### How to spot it

- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.
- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.
- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,
  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.
- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.
- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial
  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.

### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)

Until PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:

```lean
/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/
noncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=
  match g with
  | some p => p.poly
  | none   => 0
```

The consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange
interpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained
a `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.
The paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the
Lean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead
it carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for
which its conclusion was meaningless.

**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,
threads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into
`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset
as `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields
are visible at call sites.

### Acceptable uses of this pattern

Not every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances
that provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for
`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does
any theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says "the output satisfies
P", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is
smuggling a precondition.

### How to fix it

Pick one of:

1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the
   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot
   be passed.
2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle
   the case, so theorems about "the output" now quantify only over the
   `some` branch.
3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //
   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where
   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.

### Classical-logic dependencies

A sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances
that silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be
constructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`
implementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to
gate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR
#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.
Those classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely
non-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't
bottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of
classical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.

## Reviewer checklist

Use this alongside the blocker
list in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)
checklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper
result, ask:

- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the
      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.
- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If
      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match
      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.
- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if
      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature
      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.
- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an
      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness
      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.
- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a
      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it
      (A5).
- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /
      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its
      grounding plan (A6)?
- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's
      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences
      as ⚠️S in [#1379].

A lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is
scaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with
`\leanok` until the gap is closed).

## CI prevention

Mechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:

- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use
  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current
  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses
  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares
  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers
  separately. When [#438] lands (`\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same
  idea to all `\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any
  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion
  structure, warn.
- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where
  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases
  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in
  an allow-list.
- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,
  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have
  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.
- **A4 (default witnesses).** Grep `:= default`, `refine ⟨default`, `exact
  ⟨default`, `Classical.arbitrary` inside proof bodies (not typeclass
  definitions). Cross-reference to [#1379]'s witness ledger.
- **A5 (Mathlib bypass).** No reliable CI check, but `audits/` reports
  catch it during per-chapter audits.
- **A6 (external smuggles).** Every new `structure *Statement` without a
  producing theorem should be required to carry a `/-- Grounded by: #NNN
  -/` docstring, enforced by a lint rule over `blueprint/`.

The scripts in `scripts/` (notably `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py` and
`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`) are the natural home for extensions that
add these checks.

   147	/-- Coordinate restriction as a linear endomorphism. -/
   148	private def coordinateRestrictionLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   149	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) :

   151	  toFun := coordinateRestriction S
   152	  map_add' := coordinateRestriction_add S

   154	    ext a
   155	    by_cases ha : a ∈ S <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

   157	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   158	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   159	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   160	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) :
   161	    ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x = x := by
   162	  classical
   163	  ext a
   164	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   165	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   166	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   167	  · intro i _ hij
   168	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   169	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   170	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   171	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   172	
   173	private theorem sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   174	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   175	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   176	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (f : J → ι → K)
   177	    (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (x : ι → K) :
   178	    (∑ j, f j) = x ↔ ∀ j, f j = coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   179	  classical
   180	  constructor
   181	  · intro h j
   182	    rw [← h]
   183	    exact (coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint f hf j).symm
   184	  · intro h
   185	    calc
   186	      (∑ j, f j) = ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   187	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => h j
   188	      _ = x := sum_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover x

   190	/-- The value of the strict-prefix marginal preceding `k`. This is a
   191	formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-kth`, blueprint
   192	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1099`, paper
   193	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   194	def clPrefix {K ι : Type*} [Zero K] {ell : ℕ}
   195	    (marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (k : Fin ell)
   196	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
   197	  if _hk : k.val = 0 then 0
   198	  else marginal ⟨k.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) k.isLt⟩ x

   200	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
   201	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
   202	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1099`, paper
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   204	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   205	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   206	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
   207	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   208	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
   209	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   210	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/
   211	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   212	  /-- Each marginal has the corresponding conditionally linear level. -/
   213	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
   214	  /-- The selected factor registers are pairwise disjoint. -/
   215	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →
   216	    Disjoint (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) (factor j (clPrefix marginal j x))
   217	  /-- The selected factor registers cover all coordinates. -/
   218	  factor_cover : ∀ x a, ∃ i, a ∈ factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   219	  /-- Each selected linear map is supported on its factor register. -/
   220	  linear_supported : ∀ k u x a, a ∉ factor k u → linear k u x a = 0
   221	  /-- Each marginal is the sum of the preceding selected linear pieces. -/
   222	  sum_formula : ∀ k x, marginal k x =
   223	    ∑ i : Fin ell, if i.val ≤ k.val then
   224	      linear i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   225	        (coordinateRestriction (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) x) else 0
   226	  /-- The final marginal is the original function. -/
   227	  top : ∀ h : 0 < ell,
   228	    marginal ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ = L

   234	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   235	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   236	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   237	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   238	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K S (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
   239	  factor_subset : ∀ k u, factor k u ⊆ S
   240	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →
   241	    Disjoint (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x))
   242	      (factor j (clPrefix marginal j x))
   243	  factor_cover : ∀ x a, a ∈ S → ∃ i, a ∈ factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   244	  linear_supported : ∀ k u x a, a ∉ factor k u → linear k u x a = 0
   245	  sum_formula : ∀ k x, marginal k x =
   246	    ∑ i : Fin ell, if i.val ≤ k.val then
   247	      linear i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   248	        (coordinateRestriction (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) x) else 0
   249	  top : ∀ h : 0 < ell,
   250	    marginal ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ = L

   252	/-- Every marginal in support-relative decomposition data is supported on the
   253	active register. -/
   254	private theorem CLDataOn.marginal_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   255	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
   256	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (d : CLDataOn K ι S ell L)
   257	    (k : Fin ell) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
   258	    d.marginal k x a = 0 := by
   259	  rw [d.sum_formula, Finset.sum_apply]
   260	  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionUniform

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`
    14	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`), `def:cl-dist`
    15	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1067-1070`), `lem:cl-concat`
    16	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`), and `def:graph-distribution`
    17	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1233-1245`).
    18	The paper origins are
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57,282-314`,
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`,
    21	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    27	
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	
    30	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    34	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    35	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    36	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    37	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    38	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    39	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`,
    40	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    41	-/
    42	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    43	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    44	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    45	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    46	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    47	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    48	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    49	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    50	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    51	
    52	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    53	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    54	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    55	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    56	-/
    57	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    58	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    59	
    60	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    61	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    62	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    63	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    64	-/
    65	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    66	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    67	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    68	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    69	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    70	      fun x =>
    71	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    72	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    73	
    74	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    75	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    76	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    78	-/
    79	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    80	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    81	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    82	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    83	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    84	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    85	
    86	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    87	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    88	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    89	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    90	-/
    91	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    92	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    93	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    94	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    95	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    96	
    97	/--
    98	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    99	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`; paper
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
   101	-/
   102	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   103	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   104	
   105	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   106	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation
   107	construction of `lem:cl-concat`. -/
   108	private def CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   109	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : (ell : ℕ) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   110	  | 0 => .zero
   111	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)
   112	
   113	@[simp]
   114	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   115	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (x : ι → K) :
   116	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   117	  induction ell with
   118	  | zero => rfl
   119	  | succ ell ih =>
   120	      simp [CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval, ih]

   122	private theorem CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   123	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) :
   124	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   125	      (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) S := by
   126	  induction ell generalizing S with
   127	  | zero => trivial
   128	  | succ ell ih =>
   129	      exact ⟨by simp, fun _ => ih _⟩

   131	/-- Extending the support set preserves the support invariant. -/
   132	private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   133	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
   134	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S T : Finset ι}
   135	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
   136	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t T := by
   137	  induction t generalizing S T with
   138	  | zero => trivial
   139	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   140	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   141	      refine ⟨hS₁.trans hST, fun y => ih y (hrest y) ?_⟩
   142	      exact Finset.sdiff_subset_sdiff hST (fun _ h => h)

   144	/-- Lift a linear map to the left summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   145	private def condLinearLiftLeft {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]

   147	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where

   150	    ext i
   151	    cases i with
   152	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   153	    | inr i => simp
   154	  map_smul' c x := by
   155	    ext i
   156	    cases i with
   157	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   158	    | inr i => simp

   160	/-- Lift a linear map to the right summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   161	private def condLinearLiftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   162	    (L : (ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιV → K)) :
   163	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   164	  toFun x := Sum.elim 0 (L (fun i => x (.inr i)))
   165	  map_add' x y := by
   166	    ext i
   167	    cases i with
   168	    | inl i => simp
   169	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   170	  map_smul' c x := by
   171	    ext i
   172	    cases i with
   173	    | inl i => simp
   174	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i

   176	/-- Lift a representation of a conditionally linear function to the right
   177	summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   178	private def CondLinearTerm.liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   179	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] :
   180	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell →
   181	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) ell

   183	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   184	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr) (condLinearLiftRight L₁)
   185	        (by
   186	          intro x i hi
   187	          cases i with
   188	          | inl i => rfl
   189	          | inr i =>
   190	              apply hSupport
   191	              simpa using hi)

   194	@[simp]
   195	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   196	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]

   209	private theorem CondLinearTerm.liftRight_supportedOn {K ιU ιV : Type*}
   210	    [Field K] [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   211	    {ell : ℕ} {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell} {S : Finset ιV}
   212	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
   213	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.liftRight (ιU := ιU) t)

   216	  | zero => trivial

   765	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (fun b => x b)) a = x a

   565	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   566	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   567	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   568	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   569	        intro i j hij
   570	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   571	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   572	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   573	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   574	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   575	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   576	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   577	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   578	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   579	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   580	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   581	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))

   583	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]

   585	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   586	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   587	              ((t j).tail
   588	                ((t j).headLinear
   589	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   590	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   591	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]

   593	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   594	        rw [htail_eval]

   598	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   599	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   600	        funext j
   601	        rw [hselect]

   603	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   604	            (∑ j, y j) +
   605	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   606	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   607	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by

   609	                    (coordinateRestriction
   610	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   611	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   612	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   613	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   614	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   615	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   616	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   617	                            (coordinateRestriction
   618	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   619	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   620	              rw [htail_family]

   622	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   623	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   624	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   625	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   626	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   627	              intro j _

   630	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   631	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   632	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   633	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   634	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   635	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   636	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   637	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   638	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   639	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   640	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   641	  classical
   642	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   643	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   644	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   645	  funext x
   646	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   647	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   648	  intro j _
   649	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   650	
   651	/--
   652	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   653	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   654	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1067-1070`, paper origin
   655	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   656	-/
   657	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   658	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   659	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   660	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   661	
   662	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   663	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   664	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   665	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   666	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, paper origin
   667	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   668	-/
   669	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   670	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   671	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   672	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   673	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   674	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   675	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   676	
   677	/--
   678	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   679	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, with
   680	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   681	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   682	-/
   683	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   684	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   685	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   686	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   687	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   688	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   689	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   690	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   691	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   692	  classical
   693	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   694	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   695	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   696	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   697	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   698	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   699	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   700	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   701	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   702	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   703	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   704	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   705	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   706	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   707	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   708	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   709	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   710	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   711	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   712	    have huniv :
   713	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   714	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   715	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   716	      ext i
   717	      cases i <;> simp
   718	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   719	  · funext x
   720	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   721	    simp only [zero_add]
   722	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   723	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   724	    rfl

   726	/--
   727	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   728	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   729	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1233-1245`;
   730	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   731	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   732	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   733	-/
   734	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   735	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   736	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   737	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   738	
   739	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   740	nonempty.  This is not a named statement of the source article; it is
   741	`lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   742	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1257`. -/
   743	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   744	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   745	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   746	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   747	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   748	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   749	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   750	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   751

   433	private def condLinearHeadSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   434	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] {ell : ℕ}

   455	/-- Combine equal-level representations of conditionally linear functions on
   456	disjoint registers. -/
   457	private def CondLinearTerm.directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   458	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   459	    (V : J → Finset ι) :
   460	    (ell : ℕ) → (J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) →
   461	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   462	  | 0, _ => .zero
   463	  | ell + 1, t =>
   464	      .succ (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) (condLinearHeadSum t)
   465	        (by
   466	          intro x a ha
   467	          simp only [condLinearHeadSum, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
   468	            Finset.sum_apply]
   469	          apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   470	          intro j _
   471	          exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   472	            (fun haj => ha (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)))
   473	        (fun y => directSum (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   474	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y)))

   476	private theorem CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   477	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   478	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   479	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   480	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) :
   481	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t)
   482	      (Finset.univ.biUnion V) := by
   483	  induction ell generalizing V with
   484	  | zero => trivial
   485	  | succ ell ih =>
   486	      have hhead (j : J) : (t j).headSupport ⊆ V j :=
   487	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   488	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   489	      · exact Finset.biUnion_subset.mpr fun j _ =>
   490	          (hhead j).trans (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem V (Finset.mem_univ j))
   491	      · intro y
   492	        have htail (j : J) :
   493	            CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   494	              ((t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y))
   495	              (V j \ (t j).headSupport) :=
   496	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) _
   497	        have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   498	            Disjoint (V i \ (t i).headSupport) (V j \ (t j).headSupport) := by
   499	          intro i j hij
   500	          exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   501	        have hrec := ih _ hDisjointTail _ htail
   502	        have hunion :
   503	            Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) =
   504	              Finset.univ.biUnion V \
   505	                Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => (t j).headSupport) := by
   506	          ext a
   507	          constructor
   508	          · intro ha
   509	            obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp ha
   510	            obtain ⟨haV, haS⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hj
   511	            refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr
   512	              ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haV⟩, ?_⟩
   513	            intro haHeads
   514	            obtain ⟨i, _, hai⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp haHeads
   515	            by_cases hij : i = j
   516	            · subst i
   517	              exact haS hai
   518	            · exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) (hhead i hai) haV
   519	          · intro ha
   520	            obtain ⟨j, _, haV⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1
   521	            refine Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
   522	              ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨haV, ?_⟩⟩
   523	            intro haj
   524	            exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).2
   525	              (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)
   526	        simpa only [hunion] using hrec

   528	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   529	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   530	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   531	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   532	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) (x : ι → K) :
   533	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t) x =
   534	      ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   535	  induction ell generalizing V x with
   536	  | zero =>
   537	      apply Eq.symm
   538	      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   539	      intro j _
   540	      cases t j
   541	      rfl
   542	  | succ ell ih =>
   543	      let S : J → Finset ι := fun j => (t j).headSupport
   544	      let y : J → ι → K := fun j =>
   545	        (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   546	      have hS (j : J) : S j ⊆ V j :=
   547	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   548	      have hy (j : J) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) : y j a = 0 := by
   549	        exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   550	          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
   551	      have hhead :
   552	          condLinearHeadSum t
   553	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
   554	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   555	        intro j _
   556	        change (t j).headLinear
   557	            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
   558	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
   559	          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   560	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
   561	          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
   562	      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
   563	        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
   564	      have htail (j : J) :
   565	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   566	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   567	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   568	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   569	        intro i j hij
   570	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   571	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   572	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   573	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   574	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   575	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   576	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   577	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   578	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   579	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   580	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   581	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   582	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
   583	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
   584	        change (t j).headLinear
   585	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   586	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   587	              ((t j).tail
   588	                ((t j).headLinear
   589	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   590	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   591	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
   592	        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   593	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   594	        rw [htail_eval]
   595	      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
   596	        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
   597	      have htail_family :
   598	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   599	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   600	        funext j
   601	        rw [hselect]
   602	      calc
   603	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   604	            (∑ j, y j) +
   605	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   606	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   607	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
   608	              change condLinearHeadSum t
   609	                    (coordinateRestriction
   610	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   611	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   612	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   613	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   614	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   615	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   616	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   617	                            (coordinateRestriction
   618	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   619	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   620	              rw [htail_family]
   621	        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   622	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   623	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   624	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   625	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   626	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   627	              intro j _
   628	              exact (hcomponent j).symm
   629	
   630	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   631	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   632	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   633	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   634	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   635	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   636	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   637	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   638	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   639	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   640	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   641	  classical
   642	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   643	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   644	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   645	  funext x
   646	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   647	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   648	  intro j _
   649	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   650	
   651	/--
   652	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   653	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   654	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1067-1070`, paper origin
   655	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   656	-/
   657	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   658	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   659	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   660	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   661	
   662	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   663	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   664	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   665	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   666	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, paper origin
   667	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   668	-/
   669	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   670	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   671	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   672	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   673	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   674	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   675	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   676	
   677	/--
   678	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   679	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1103-1117`, with
   680	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   681	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   682	-/
   683	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   684	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   685	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   686	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   687	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   688	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   689	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   690	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   691	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   692	  classical
   693	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   694	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   695	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   696	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   697	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   698	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   699	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   700	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   701	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   702	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   703	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   704	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   705	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   706	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   707	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   708	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   709	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   710	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   711	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   712	    have huniv :
   713	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   714	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   715	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   716	      ext i
   717	      cases i <;> simp
   718	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   719	  · funext x
   720	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   721	    simp only [zero_add]
   722	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   723	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   724	    rfl
   725	
   726	/--
   727	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   728	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   729	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1233-1245`;
   730	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   731	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   732	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   733	-/
   734	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   735	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   736	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   737	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   738	
   739	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   740	nonempty.  This is not a named statement of the source article; it is
   741	`lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   742	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1257`. -/
   743	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   744	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   745	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   746	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   747	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   748	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   749	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   750	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   751	
   752	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    24	/-- Add one empty first stage to a representation of a conditionally linear
    25	function. -/
    26	private def CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    27	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    28	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) :=
    29	  .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => t)

    31	@[simp]

    45	/-- Raise a representation of a conditionally linear function by a specified
    46	number of empty stages. -/
    47	private def CondLinearTerm.raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    48	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    49	    (d : ℕ) → {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell →

    54	@[simp]

    57	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :

    63	private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]

    72	/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
    73	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    74	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
    75	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    76	    (h : ell ≤ k) : IsCondLinearOn K S k L := by
    77	  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
    78	  have hk : ell + (k - ell) = k := Nat.add_sub_of_le h
    79	  rw [← hk]
    80	  exact ⟨CondLinearTerm.raiseBy (k - ell) t,
    81	    CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn _ ht,
    82	    funext fun x => by rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy, congrFun ht_eval x]⟩

    84	/-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` has values supported on `S`. -/
    85	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]

    91	  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem ht x ha

    95	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    96	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
    97	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    98	    (x : ι → K) : L (coordinateRestriction S x) = L x := by

   103	/-- Prepend one supported linear stage to a family of residual
   104	conditionally-linear maps. -/
   105	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.cons {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   106	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S S₁ : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
   107	    (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   108	    (hS₁ : S₁ ⊆ S) (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
   109	    (R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K))

   118	  change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
   119	      CondLinearTerm.eval (t (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _

   147	/-- Coordinate restriction as a linear endomorphism. -/
   148	private def coordinateRestrictionLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   149	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) :
   150	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where

   152	  map_add' := coordinateRestriction_add S

   157	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   158	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   159	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   160	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) :
   161	    ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x = x := by
   162	  classical
   163	  ext a
   164	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   165	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   166	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   167	  · intro i _ hij
   168	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   169	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   170	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   171	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim

   173	private theorem sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   174	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   175	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   176	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (f : J → ι → K)
   177	    (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (x : ι → K) :
   178	    (∑ j, f j) = x ↔ ∀ j, f j = coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   179	  classical
   180	  constructor
   181	  · intro h j
   182	    rw [← h]
   183	    exact (coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint f hf j).symm
   184	  · intro h
   185	    calc
   186	      (∑ j, f j) = ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   187	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => h j
   188	      _ = x := sum_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover x
   189	
   190	/-- The value of the strict-prefix marginal preceding `k`. This is a
   191	formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-kth`, blueprint
   192	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1099`, paper
   193	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   194	def clPrefix {K ι : Type*} [Zero K] {ell : ℕ}
   195	    (marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (k : Fin ell)
   196	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
   197	  if _hk : k.val = 0 then 0
   198	  else marginal ⟨k.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) k.isLt⟩ x
   199	
   200	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
   201	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
   202	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1099`, paper
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   204	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   205	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   206	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
   207	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   208	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
   209	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   210	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/
   211	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   212	  /-- Each marginal has the corresponding conditionally linear level. -/
   213	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
   214	  /-- The selected factor registers are pairwise disjoint. -/
   215	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →

   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show

   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,

  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.

275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}
